findings.passage: In a turbulent time where voting and constitutional rights are being threatened, I will work to ensure that both are kept intact for all of the constituents in District 12.
findings.note: Campaign issues page, general statement on protecting voting rights. No mention of ID or citizenship proof.

findings.passage: So to me, as long as a postmark exists, the ballot should be counted. I don't know why you would want to limit any votes, because if you're a strong candidate, those votes would be for you, presumably, so it should just add to your count. But it literally will disenfranchise [the] voting [rights] of military personnel.
findings.note: On a call-in radio show, she says mail ballots with a postmark should be counted, and that limiting the mail-in window would hurt military voters. Related to mail voting; it does not mention ID.

findings.passage: I think that has come to light with the ballot bill he is trying to put through. He does not want mail-in ballots past election day, which totally impedes military people — especially military people who are deployed.
findings.note: Quoted in a Daily Egyptian interview, she criticizes her opponent's ballot bill over mail-ballot deadlines. The article itself separately describes the SAVE ACT, H.R. 22, as requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register; that description is the reporter's, and she does not discuss proof of citizenship herself.

findings.passage: I am a proponent of the Second Amendment. I agree that it is part of the Second Amendment and people have a right to own guns. I have no problem with that. I also believe that there has to be some regulation. It's no different than owning or driving a car.
findings.note: Radio interview (WILL 21st Show, page dated Aug 18, 2026). She says she supports the right to own guns and also wants some regulation.
subjects: general statement on gun rights and the Second Amendment

findings.passage: And so, you know, saying that they should be able to walk into a gun store and buy a gun and ammo the same day without any kind of background check or anything — I think we've gotten to the point where we know, in this society, in our country, that safety-wise, that's just not [wise] anymore.
findings.note: Same interview. She says buying a gun and ammunition the same day with no background check is no longer wise.

findings.passage: I think they actually need to look at the facts, because we're not. Nobody has asked to go take away their weapons. Nobody has. It's just wanting to have smart legislation for them. I don't think that is asking too much at all. You know, and to me, even protecting — I don't know how law enforcement would view this, but do they want everybody on their streets who might not be mentally sound enough to have a weapon to go out and be able to buy a weapon? I don't know. I would think they wouldn't.
findings.note: Same interview, answering a question on voters who fear gun confiscation. She says no one is taking guns away, wants smart legislation, and raises limits on buyers who may not be mentally sound.
subjects: limits on who may have a gun

findings.passage: I believe the Second Amendment is a fundamental constitutional right, and I support responsible gun ownership. I will back common-sense measures that keep firearms out of the hands of dangerous individuals without infringing on the rights of law-abiding citizens. I also support education and safety initiatives that promote responsible firearm use.
findings.note: Campaign priorities page, Second Amendment section; page carries a 2026 copyright and no posting date.
subjects: general statement on gun rights and the Second Amendment

findings.passage: Respect Second Amendment rights while promoting responsible gun safety
findings.note: Campaign press kit, fact sheet list of priority issues (page 3). The same page lists Gun Sense Voter among her endorsements. No posting date.
subjects: general statement on gun rights and the Second Amendment
